story.value: Californium was first produced in 1950 by Stanley G. Thompson, Glenn T. Seaborg, Kenneth Street, Jr. and Albert Ghiorso.
The scientists who first produced californium worked at the University of California, Berkeley.
Californium was first made using a device known as a cyclotron.

uses.value: A form of californium is used as a neutron source to help identify gold and silver ores.
A form of californium is used in neutron moisture gauges, which help find water and oil bearing layers in oil wells.
